newsitem.title: USA: FCC modifies merger of class-ring makers.
newsitem.headline: FCC modifies merger of class-ring makers.

text.p: The Federal Trade Commission Tuesday modified a planned merger of class-ring makers, citing a risk of higher prices to the 1.6 million high school and college graduates who buy rings every year.

The merger would have violated U.S. antitrust law by joining the number two and three makers of the commemorative rings, which would control the prices of 45 percent of all class rings sold and 90 percent of those sold in retail stores, the FTC said.

The agency said class rings range in price from $60 to more than $400, and 50-60 percent of graduating high school students buy them each year either through in-school representatives or at retail stores. No figures were given for college graduates.

Originally, Class Rings Inc., owned by Castle Harlan Partners, II, L.P., was to buy the class ring businesses of both Town & Country Corp., the number three ring company, including its L.G. Balfour Co. Inc. and Gold Lance Inc. units. It was also to purchase CJC Holdings Inc., the number two maker, which markets Art Carved and R. Johns brand rings.
The deal was worth $180 million, the agency said.
Under the negotiated amended deal, the merger will no longer include Gold Lance Inc., which will remain an independent competitor, the FTC said.
